blocks.text: Acyl chlorides have the functional group –COCl. Saturated aliphatic acyl chlorides have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COCl. According to the IUPAC system, they are named as alkanoyl halides. For example

blocks.alt: Ethanoyl chloride, CH3-C(=O)-Cl, and propanoyl chloride, CH3-CH2-C(=O)-Cl, with the O drawn above the carbonyl carbon.
blocks.caption: Ethanoyl chloride and propanoyl chloride (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 114).

blocks.text: Since acyl chlorides are the most reactive compounds among the functional derivatives of carboxylic acids, they are usually prepared in such a way that they can be used for the preparation of other functional derivatives.
